transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

The things that used to mean everything to me—my garden, my quilts, my walks—don’t matter anymore, and I can’t make myself care about any of it. I just feel completely flat, and I don't know how to find the spark to care about anything anymore.
Have you had other episodes in the past where you felt depressed or lost interest like this for at least two weeks, or is this the first time it has happened?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is definitely the first time it has ever been this bad, and it all really started after my sister passed away.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself? If so, have you made any plans?

Almost every day now, I find myself thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. I've even pictured taking all my old pain pills at once so I could stop being a burden to everyone, though that thought really scares me afterward.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t, or felt certain of things like being to blame or beyond help even when others say that isn’t true?

Yes, when the house is quiet at night, I clearly hear my sister's voice calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should come with her. I also feel like a terrible, useless person because I am convinced that her death and all the bad things that have happened are entirely my fault, even though my daughter tells me otherwise.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime episode of major depression with clear depressed mood/anhedonia, recurrent suicidal ideation with overdose plan, and psychotic symptoms consisting of auditory hallucinations and delusional/excessive guilt. No prior episodes were reported, supporting a single severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
